mcp-bouncer - a bouncer for MCP servers

USAGE
  mcp-bouncer --policy policy.json -- <server command...>   wrap a stdio MCP server
  mcp-bouncer scan -- <server command...>                   audit its tools and exit
  mcp-bouncer gen                                           print a starter policy

POLICY (JSON)
  {
    "audit": "bouncer-audit.jsonl",
    "tools": {
      "read_file": { "args": { "path": { "kind": "path", "allow": ["./**"], "deny": ["**/.env", "**/.ssh/**"] } } },
      "get_env":   { "allow": false },
      "fetch":     { "args": { "url": { "kind": "url", "allowSchemes": ["https:"] } } },
      "resources/read": { "allow": false }
    },
    "rateLimitPerMin": { "*": 60 },
    "maxResponseBytes": 1000000
  }
Tools not listed are blocked AND hidden from tools/list (set "defaultAllow": true to flip).
Request methods are gated too: resources/list, prompts/get, completion/complete etc. need a
"tools" entry (e.g. "prompts/list": {"allow": true}) or defaultAllow. Lifecycle methods
(initialize, ping, notifications/*) always pass.
"../" escapes, absolute paths, IPv6/private/SSRF URLs, batches, and id-less calls all fail closed.
